title: Legal + Procurement: LLM Pilot Gate & MSA/DPA Clarification
summary: Kickoff between procurement/legal and Redwood for an initial LLM pilot. Primary focus on MSA/DPA redlines, SLA expectations (p95 latency / uptime), pricing model and egress costs, and onboarding checklist for a 6-week pilot. Agreed next steps: share MSA-friendly template, run latency benchmarks, security deep-dive scheduling.
topics: SLA: latency p95 and uptime SLOs
Pricing for pilot and enterprise pricing approval path
Onboarding timeline and pilot acceptance criteria

Priya Nair - Share data classification matrix and whether any data must remain in-region (EU) - due 2026-04-07

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-04 15:30 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ethan Brooks (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (Redwood SE), Damon Lee (Stratalytics VP Procurement), Priya Nair (Head of Security), Omar Ruiz (ML Platform Lead), Sara Kim (Legal)

Summary: Quick kickoff to align procurement/legal + infra on the pilot gating items: MSA/DPA, SLAs, pricing approvals, and security checks.

Topics: MSA redlines, DPA retention, SLA targets, pricing and egress, KMS choices, pilot acceptance criteria.

Action items (captured in notes): see metadata.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for making time today, um this should be a quick kickoff to align legal and procurement items for the pilot.
[00:12] Damon Lee: Yeah thanks Maya. We wanted to make sure the MSA/DPA pathway is clear, and get a traffic light on pricing and SLAs before exec budget sign-off.
[00:23] Ethan Brooks: Hi, Ethan here — I'll be doing the technical benchmarks, latency numbers, and the pilot runbook. Quick note — Redwood provides Hosted, Dedicated and Private options; for pilots customers often start Hosted then move to Dedicated if they need predictable throughput.
[00:40] Priya Nair: Right, from security we'll need SOC 2 evidence, encryption in transit and at rest, and clarification on KMS / bring-your-own-key. Also data residency — some EU user PII needs to stay in region.
[00:56] Maya Chen: Absolutely. For KMS we offer both managed keys and BYOK via customer KMS (we can support HSM-backed flows), though the exact flow depends on Private vs Dedicated, and there are slightly different entitlements for audit logs and key-wrapping.
[01:15] Sara Kim: When you say BYOK, can you confirm whether Redwood has any ability to decrypt or access the customer keys for troubleshooting? That will be a legal redline if yes.
[01:25] Lena Ortiz: Short answer: with BYOK we don't have plaintext access to your private key; we handle key references and orchestration but the keys live in your KMS. For some troubleshooting we can request temporary audit traces but not key material. I'll follow up with the security doc link.
[01:42] Omar Ruiz: On the performance side — our workload is short chat-like queries but high QPS; we care about p95 latency under 180ms and cold-starts under 600ms. How do you typically ensure that?
[01:58] Ethan Brooks: Good question. Our serving runtime uses continuous batching and KV cache reuse; for chat flows that reuse contexts we get big wins. For Dedicated you can pin model variants and have reserved capacity to hit tighter p95s. We'll run a sim with your sample dataset — that's an action item.
[02:20] Damon Lee: Pricing is the sticking point for procurement. We need to know: pilot pricing, egress fees, and what happens if we scale to 1B tokens/month. Also, what are the approved discount bands and procurement approval path?
[02:36] Maya Chen: For pilots we usually provide a time-boxed pilot discount and usage credits; for scale we have tiered unit pricing and reserved capacity pricing for Dedicated. I'll send a cost model showing hosted vs dedicated, token-unit assumptions, and egress scenarios.
[02:53] Priya Nair: Also are there any data processing addendums re: sub-processors? We need a list of infra sub-providers.
[03:04] Maya Chen: Yes, we can provide a subprocessor list and a DPA checklist. We'll attach a standard DPA which lists common cloud infra partners; if you require fixed-residency infra we can discuss Private deployment.
[03:17] Sara Kim: On the MSA — our legal team will likely ask for audit rights, indemnity language tweaks, and limits on data retention. Are there standard MSA exceptions Redwood is willing to accept?
[03:28] Maya Chen: We normally accept negotiation on data retention and specific clauses around audit rights. We have a playbook for enterprise redlines — some clauses require exec approval. If you send your top three must-haves, we can route to Legal and come back with green/amber/red on each.
[03:43] Damon Lee: Timeline: we want procurement approval before end of April to kick off a May pilot. Is that feasible?
[03:51] Ethan Brooks: Technically yes — assuming legal signoff and we get sample data for benchmarking quickly. Pilot onboarding takes ~1–2 weeks to stand up and validate.
[04:06] Priya Nair: A technical point, are you supporting VPC peering or private endpoints? For Private deployment we need VPC peering and dedicated network paths.
[04:15] Lena Ortiz: We support VPC peering and customer-hosted Private deployments. For Hosted we provide TLS endpoints; Dedicated offers private networking and optional VPC peering. There are different SLA tiers per deployment model.
[04:29] Omar Ruiz: If we do Dedicated, what's the billing cadence — monthly reserved commit vs upfront annual?
[04:36] Maya Chen: Reserved capacity is typically monthly or annual commits; the exact terms can be flexible and tied to committed throughput. We'll include example contracts in the packet.
[04:47] Sara Kim: Are there any known compliance certifications beyond SOC 2? HIPAA? ISO?
[04:53] Maya Chen: We have SOC 2 Type II and are pursuing ISO 27001; HIPAA support is available via BAAs for certain contracts. We'll send the current compliance matrix.
[05:05] Damon Lee: Great. On liability and indemnity — we need a clearer limit of liability for data breaches tied to negligence.
[05:12] Maya Chen: Understood — that's one of the legal items we'll escalate; your counsel's proposed wording will help us route.
[05:18] Priya Nair: For the pilot acceptance criteria — what are the success metrics? We'll share ours but suggest: p95 latency < 200ms, uptime 99.5 during pilot window, and classification accuracy within tolerances.
[05:33] Ethan Brooks: That sounds reasonable. We recommend a runbook that captures load profile, prompt sets, and eval harness. We'll help define the pass/fail criteria.
[05:44] Damon Lee: If we sign a short pilot MSA, can you limit the data retention to 30 days and provide deletion certs?
[05:51] Maya Chen: Yes — DPA clauses can specify retention windows and deletion certifications for pilot data. We'll note that on the redline template.
[06:00] Sara Kim: A small nit — can Redwood provide logs for tokens and request traces for a 90-day window? We need traceability for audits.
[06:09] Lena Ortiz: We can provide per-request telemetry and audit logs; retention windows can be extended as part of an add-on. There may be cost and privacy tradeoffs.
[06:19] Damon Lee: Back to pricing — what's the egress policy? If we have 3rd party storage, is there extra transfer cost?
[06:26] Maya Chen: Egress policies vary by cloud region and deployment. We'll model egress scenarios; typically egress to same cloud region is cheaper, cross-region or cross-cloud has fees. We'll provide an egress matrix.
[06:36] Omar Ruiz: Are we able to get a temporary test tenant with RBAC and SSO to exercise integration?
[06:43] Ethan Brooks: Yes — we can spin a sandbox with SAML SSO and token-level RBAC for the pilot. We'll coordinate on SSO metadata exchange.
[06:51] Priya Nair: On encryption, we need FIPS-compliant ciphers and key rotation policies documented.
[06:58] Lena Ortiz: Noted — we'll include cipher suites and key rotation in the security doc.
[07:05] Damon Lee: Can we get a short readout on rollback and graceful degradation — e.g., what happens if model variant is unavailable?
[07:12] Ethan Brooks: Platform supports smart routing and automatic fallback to compatible variants. For Dedicated we can configure canaries and automatic fallback policy. We'll document typical failure modes.
[07:25] Sara Kim: When you mention telemetry, will Redwood store PII in logs? That's a no-go.
[07:32] Maya Chen: No PII should be stored in logs by default; we can scrub or redact tokens in logs based on your DPA.
[07:41] Damon Lee: Ok, so next steps — can we capture the immediate actions?
[07:46] Maya Chen: Sure. Action items recap: we'll send MSA & DPA redline-friendly templates and security docs; Ethan will run the latency sim; Stratalytics will send data classification and top MSA redlines; we'll schedule the security deep-dive.
[07:59] Priya Nair: Sounds good. Also please include the subprocessor list and compliance evidence.
[08:05] Maya Chen: Will do.
[08:08] Omar Ruiz: One more technical: will you provide a limited-support SLA during pilot? We need someone we can page.
[08:15] Maya Chen: Yes — for pilots we provide an onboarding SE + on-call for critical issues; if you move to Dedicated there's a named SE and higher SLA options.
[08:26] Sara Kim: We'll prepare our redlines and legal notes and share them by the dates discussed.
[08:32] Damon Lee: Great, thanks all.
[08:35] Maya Chen: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with the docs and schedule.
[08:39] [call ends]

Notes on transcription: some words may be mis-attributed; product names like "KV cache" were occasionally transcribed as "K V cash". Speakers occasionally talk over each other; timestamps approximate.
